sentences.text:
This petition under Article 226 of Constitution of India has been filed seeking the following reliefs:-
i.
This, Hon'ble Court may kindly pleased to call for relevant record pertaining to subject matter for kind perusal of this Hon'ble Court.

ii. It is therefore, prayed that the Hon'ble Court may be pleased to issue a writ in the nature of mandamus directing the respondents/depts to the pay the compensation against the acquisition of house/land of minor petitioners mentioned in the objections contained in Ann.P/1 to Ann.P/4 adjudicating the grievances raised by them within stipulate period by granting the compensation at the prevalent market rate mentioned in the guidelines of Collector with interst @18% p.a. iii.

This, Hon'ble Court may kindly pleased issue any other Writ, directions, orders which this Hon'ble Court may deems fit and proper, looking to the facts and circumstances of the case together cost of petition.

It is submitted by counsel for petitioners that the land belonging to the petitioners i.e. Khasra No.
394, area 1.480 hectors was acquired for construction of Lalitpur Singrauli Railway Line.

However,
the said compensation has been paid to one Jai Singh Gond, S/o Ramlakhan Gond, Lalbahadur Singh, S/o Bhukhan Singh Gond and Maheep Singh, S/o Lalbahadur Singh Gond and accordingly, it is prayed that the compensation for the said land be paid to the petitioners.

3. Heard learned counsel for the petitioners.

sentences.text: It appears that certain lands were acquired by the respondents under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency inLand Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency inLand Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 5. If a person is of the view that the compensation has been paid to a wrong person, then the same can be a ground for making reference under Section 64 of Act, 2013.

6. Accordingly, this Court is of considered opinion that since the entitlement of a person to receive compensation is a disputed question of fact which can be adjudicated by leading evidence, therefore,
the petitioner has an efficacious remedy under Section 64 of Act, 2013.
7. With aforesaid liberty, the petition is dismissed.

8. It is made clear that this Court has not considered the merits of the case and in case if reference is preferred, then it shall be decided in accordance with law without getting influenced or prejudiced by this order.

(G.S. AHLUWALIA) JUDGE AL 3 WP-18021-2024 Manoj Singh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184114351/
